title: Do six equilateral triangles make a regular hexagon?
description: Six congruent equilateral triangles are placed round a centre O. Six angles of sixty degrees fill the full angle of three hundred and sixty degrees, so there is no gap and no overlap, and the outer figure is a regular hexagon. Keeko's doubt, a small gap after the sixth triangle, is tested and struck out.
teaching_notes: One idea: angles that add to three hundred and sixty degrees fill the space round a point exactly. Watch for students who trust the look of a drawing instead of adding the angles.

source: Six congruent equilateral triangles are placed round a centre O.
video_script.why: The child knows the angles of an equilateral triangle and a full turn, but has not yet used them to see why six triangles fit round a point.
video_script.substitution: Angles that add up to a full angle fill the space round a point with no gap and no overlap.
video_script.anchor: Six congruent equilateral triangles are placed round a centre O: do they fit with no gap and no overlap, and is the outer figure a regular hexagon?
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks a small gap is left after the sixth triangle, because shapes never fit perfectly. Six angles of 60 degrees add to exactly 360 degrees, so no gap is left.
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, the six triangles fit, and the outer shape is a regular hexagon

final_answer.value: Yes: six 60° angles make 360°, so they fit; the hexagon has equal sides and every angle is 120°
final_answer.spoken: yes, six sixty degree angles make three hundred and sixty degrees, so they fit; the hexagon has equal sides and every angle is one hundred and twenty degrees

never_show: the finished hexagon outline before step three
maths_rules: Each angle of an equilateral triangle is 60 degrees.
At O, six such angles meet, and 6 x 60 = 360, the full angle round a point, so there is no gap and no overlap.
The six outer sides are sides of congruent triangles, so they are all equal.
At each outer corner two angles of 60 degrees meet, making 60 + 60 = 120 degrees, so all six angles are equal.
Equal sides and equal angles make the outer figure a regular hexagon.
Slip: a gap is not left, because the sum is exactly 360.
video_script.design: One idea: add the angles round O. Keeko's doubt is a small gap after the sixth triangle. The hexagon outline appears only after the outer sides and corners are checked.
